newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end lacklustre Tokyo trade unchanged.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end lacklustre Tokyo trade unchanged.

text.p: Key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Monday's Tokyo session flat. Volume was an extremely thin 23,337 contracts.

The March contract rose as high as 126.62 shortly after the open, following Friday's rise in U.S. Treasuries and weekend media reports that Sakura Bank Ltd had rejected a rehabilitation plan proposed by trouble loan firm Apollo Leasing Co, traders said.
However, the March closed unchanged at an intraday low of 126.35, as a lack of follow-through buying prompted dealers to liquidate longs in the afternoon, they said.
"Weak stocks were supportive, but today's decline in the Nikkei was not big enough to stimulate buying in JGBs," said a trader at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended down 244.06 points or 1.33 percent at 18,085.95, managing to remain above 18,000 throughout the session.
Market participants were cautious ahead of JNR Settlement Corp's land auction results announcement at 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), traders said.
The auction covers some 53,000 sq metres of idle land once owned by the now-defunct Japanese National Railways (JNR).
A strong auction result could boost sentiment in Japan's sluggish property market, which would be positive for stocks but negative for JGBs, traders said.
Important forthcoming events both here and overseas were also making players cautious about testing higher levels.
Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita is scheduled to speak at an economic symposium in Tokyo on Tuesday.
Players will be also watching the outcome of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in the United States on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Short-covering pressure ahead of an expected change in the benchmark futures contract from March to June was likely to help limit the downside, a brokerage house trader said.
"The change in the benchmark could take place later this month, so short-covering pressure for the March contract is likely to intensify next week," he said.
Traders said the demand-supply balance remained favourable as investors were still keen to buy cash JGBs on dips.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.375 percent as of 4.20 p.m. (0720 GMT), down from 2.385 percent on Friday.
New corporate bond issues to be launched this week were also likely to meet healthy demand, traders said.
